title: Dominic and the Promise
premise: Coral Halloran, a marine biologist who fled his old life and name eleven years ago after a betrayal that cost him everything, has built a careful existence on Merrow Island counting sea turtles and keeping everyone at arm's length. When a storm unearths a letter he never received—postmarked the week he disappeared, written by Dominic Ashe, the man who once loved him and whom Coral abandoned to save himself—Coral learns Dominic never stopped searching for him. Now Dominic arrives on the island as the lead consultant on a development project that threatens both the turtle nesting grounds and Coral's fragile sanctuary, forcing the two men into proximity neither can escape. As Coral's research becomes the last line of defense for the beach, he must decide whether to keep hiding behind the identity that kept him alive or claim his real name, his history, and Dominic's love before the project—and time—run out; in the end, Coral testifies publicly under his true name, saves the nesting grounds, and chooses Dominic, accepting that belonging requires being fully seen.
about_author: Xanthe Montrose is the pen name of a former field researcher who spent five seasons on remote coastal stations before turning to fiction. They write love stories about people who rebuild themselves far from where they started.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Dawn survey on Merrow Island: Coral logs a green turtle nest, savoring the ritual that structures his safe life. Introduce his routines, his chosen name, and his refusal to talk about his past. Emotional beat: contentment built on avoidance.

chapters.title: What the Storm Brought Up
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Post-storm beach cleanup uncovers a waterlogged mail sack lost in a depot flood years ago; among it, an envelope addressed to a name Coral buried—his birth name. He pockets it without opening it. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Tide
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with flashback fragments. Alone in his cottage, Coral holds the unopened letter through the night, remembering only in flashes: a city, a fire, a choice he made running. He doesn't read it yet. Beat: fear tightening its grip.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He finally reads Dominic's eleven-year-old letter—an apology, an address, an open door. The return address is long dead. Coral burns nothing but sleeps badly. Beat: grief for a life interrupted.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tries to resume normalcy: lab work, tea with landlady Maren, teaching local kids about hatchlings. But he checks the ferry schedule twice. Beat: the past leaking into the present.

chapters.title: The Man from the Mainland
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV introduced. Dominic Ashe steps off the ferry as coastal development consultant for the Merrow Point resort proposal, telling himself this assignment is coincidence. He doesn't know Coral is here. Beat: hope wearing a professional mask.

chapters.title: First Sightings
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Coral and Dominic nearly collide at the community meeting about the development; recognition hits them both like cold water. Neither says a word in public. Beat: shock, denial, electric awareness.

chapters.title: You're Dead to Me Was Never True
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic confronts Coral privately on the dune path. Eleven years of anger and relief spill out; Coral gives him nothing but logistics. Beat: collision without resolution.

chapters.title: Nesting Season Rules
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral throws himself into opposing the resort, drafting ecological impact arguments. His data is strong but his standing is thin—he's a newcomer with no institutional weight. Beat: purpose as armor.

chapters.title: Dinner Under Protest
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Forced together by the assessment process, they share an awkward meal at Maren's pub. Dominic notices Coral flinches at his old name; he starts using 'Coral' deliberately. Beat: first crack in hostility.

chapters.title: What I Ran From
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, extended flashback chapter. Full reveal: Coral testified against his powerful family's fraud scheme, was disowned and threatened, faked a clean break, and let Dominic believe he'd simply left him. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Half a Confession
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On a night survey, Coral tells Dominic a partial truth—that he was protecting someone by disappearing—but not that Dominic was the someone. Dominic sees the evasion clearly. Beat: intimacy shadowed by omission.

chapters.title: The Consultant's Report
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic's preliminary findings could go either way; his firm expects approval. He begins quietly documenting environmental problems, knowing it may end his career. Beat: loyalty shifting sides.

chapters.title: Hatchling Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The first nest erupts at midnight; Coral lets Dominic help guide hatchlings to the sea. In the dark, hands touch, defenses drop, and they almost kiss. Beat: tenderness breaking through.

chapters.title: Maren Knows Everything
chapters.summary: Maren's brief POV interlude. The landlady, who took Coral in years ago, recognizes what Dominic is to him and warns each man separately: island life punishes half-truths. Beat: outside perspective on their stalling.

chapters.title: Old Name, New Wound
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic digs into why Coral vanished and finds news archives: the trial, the threats, the erasure. He realizes Coral sacrificed everything—including him—to survive. Beat: anger transmuting into heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The developer offers Coral a paid consultancy to endorse a 'mitigated' plan—money, legitimacy, protection from his past if anyone comes looking. Tempted, he almost signs. Beat: the devil offering safety.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral declines and instead hands Dominic evidence that the developer's environmental surveys were falsified. Trusting Dominic with this is the first risk he's taken in years. Beat: alliance sealed in secret.

chapters.title: Working Nights
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Building the case together, they fall into rhythm—shared thermoses, shared silences, shared laughter. Both feel the relationship tipping past friendship. Beat: falling in love in increments.

chapters.title: Kiss at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. After a breakthrough finding, Dominic kisses Coral on the empty tidal flats. Coral kisses back, then pulls away, terrified: loving someone means having something to lose again. Beat: joy colliding with fear.

chapters.title: Someone Is Asking Questions
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A private investigator hired by the developer—or possibly Coral's family—starts sniffing around the island, asking about a witness who changed his name. Coral's paranoia ignites. Beat: the past closing in.

chapters.title: Running Instincts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Old reflexes take over: Coral drafts an exit plan, packs a bag, prepares to vanish again. He pushes Dominic away cruelly to make leaving easier. Beat: self-sabotage as self-protection.

chapters.title: You Don't Get to Save Me By Leaving
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic refuses the push-out, confronting Coral: he spent eleven years grieving a coward when the truth was a martyr. He demands the whole story or nothing. Beat: ultimatum born of love.

chapters.title: The Whole Story
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral finally tells Dominic everything—the testimony, the threats, how leaving him was the cruelest price of staying alive. Dominic listens all night. Beat: catharsis; the wall comes down.

chapters.title: Belonging, Briefly
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. One perfect day: they are openly together, planning a future, mapping a life where Coral testifies again under his real name. Beat: happiness earned and fragile.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic's falsified-survey evidence reaches the developer, who retaliates: Dominic is suspended, and the investigator leaks Coral's identity to a mainland tabloid. Beat: everything at once unraveling.

chapters.title: Front Page Ghost
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The story breaks: 'Missing Witness Found Hiding on Turtle Island.' Island neighbors read his history over breakfast. Coral braces for exile and finds Maren and the locals circling protectively instead. Beat: shame met by unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Hearing Notice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The regional planning board schedules the final development hearing—and subpoenas Coral as expert witness, meaning public testimony under his legal name. Beat: the choice made concrete.

chapters.title: Flight Reflex
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The night before, panic wins: Coral stands at the ferry dock with his bag as the boat comes in. Beat: darkest moment; the old self winning.

chapters.title: The Person Who Sees Clearly
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic finds him at the dock and doesn't argue—he simply says he'll be in the hearing room either way, and that Coral surviving was never the betrayal; hiding is. The ferry passes. Beat: love as anchor, not cage.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax part one: Coral takes the stand under his full birth name, presents the falsified surveys and nesting data, and reclaims his history aloud. The developer's lawyer attacks his credibility; he holds. Beat: courage as identity.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic, defying suspension, submits corroborating evidence and testifies to the falsification chain. The two men stand as one record. Beat: partnership proven in public.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The board rejects the resort permit pending criminal investigation of the developer; the nesting grounds are protected. Outside, Dominic waits. Beat: victory, quiet and enormous.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic resigns from the firm rather than fight reinstatement, untethered for the first time. He asks Coral—not the island, not the cause—to be his reason to stay. Beat: vulnerability answered.

chapters.title: Real Name, Said Softly
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tells Dominic his birth name in private, not as a wound but as a gift, and asks him to use it sometimes. Grief and love finally share a room. Beat: integration of past and present.

chapters.title: Nest Census, Together
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Episodic domestic chapter: a season of surveys side by side, the town warming to them, small rituals becoming shared ones. Beat: belonging demonstrated in ordinary days.

chapters.title: The Letter, Answered
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral writes a reply to the eleven-year-old letter and reads it aloud at Dominic's door—a formal answer to a question asked a decade late. Yes. Beat: closure made ceremonial.

chapters.title: Threats Recede
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. News arrives: the family associate behind the investigator is indicted; the danger legally ends. Coral realizes he's been waiting for permission to live and stops waiting. Beat: release.

chapters.title: First Light
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dawn on the beach as a new nest hatches; Dominic asks Coral to build a life here with him—house, station, seasons. Coral says yes without calculating the risk. Beat: commitment without fear.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Both POVs braided. Final chapter: a year later, the research station bears a plaque with Coral's true name and Dominic's beside it. Coral counts turtles; Dominic counts the ways he stayed. Closing beat: survival was the beginning; being seen is the life.
